targets.authors: Elyousfi F, Anand A, Dalmasso A
targets.title: Impact of e-leadership and team dynamics on virtual team performance in a public organization.
targets.evidence_quote: This study replicates Elyousfi et al. (Int J Public Sect Manage 34(5):508–52814, 2021) in a novel context by examining perceived e-leadership and team dynamics in Japanese small-and-medium sized enterprises (SMEs) during the COVID-19 pandemic.
targets.outcome_quote: This study replicates Elyousfi et al. (Int J Public Sect Manage 34(5):508–52814, 2021) in a novel context by examining perceived e-leadership and team dynamics in Japanese small-and-medium sized enterprises (SMEs) during the COVID-19 pandemic. While the original study identified both constructs as drivers of virtual team performance in public-sector settings, our findings reveal a critical divergence: in crisis-driven SMEs, perceived team dynamics – encompassing collaboration, support, and cohesion – emerge as the strongest predictor of work-from-home (WFH) performance, with perceived e-leadership showing no significant direct effect.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The original found both leadership and team dynamics predicted performance; the replication supports team dynamics but explicitly contrasts the null e-leadership effect.
